statement_verbatim: On the rooted d-ary tree, place one sleeping frog at each vertex and an active frog at the root; active frogs perform independent simple random walks and wake every frog they visit. Decide for d = 3 and d = 4 whether the root is visited infinitely often almost surely (recurrence) or finitely often (transience).
locator: HJJ Theorem 1 and Conjecture 2, manuscript pp. 2–3

best_known.bound or case: One-frog simple-random-walk model: recurrent on T_2; transient on T_d for every integer d >= 5.
Recurrence for d=3 and transience for d=4 are conjectured, based on simulations.
For all sufficiently large d, the Poisson critical density satisfies 0.24 d <= mu_c(d) <= 2.28 d.
best_known.citation: Johnson and Junge, The critical density for the frog model is the degree of the tree, ECP 21 (2016), paper 82; arXiv:1607.07914

best_known.bound or case: For one frog per site with inward drift p, p_d <= 42/145 for d>=3 and p_d <= 40/153 for d>=4. These are greater than unbiased p=1/4 and p=1/5 respectively and do not classify T3 or T4.
best_known.citation: Poly Mathews Jr., Improved critical drift estimates for the frog model on trees, ECP 29 (2024); arXiv:2309.14443v2; DOI 10.1214/24-ECP606
best_known.locator: Introduction p. 2 and Theorem 1 table p. 3; S_m=sup_{d>=m}p_d

best_known.bound or case: The one-frog simple-random-walk model is recurrent on the 3,2-alternating tree, with 3 children at even depths and 2 children at odd depths. This is a different tree and does not settle T3.
best_known.citation: Josh Rosenberg, Recurrence of the frog model on the 3,2-alternating tree, arXiv:1701.02813

best_known.bound or case: Already-known ordinary p_d>=1/(d+1), by the all-particles-initially-active upper process; specifically p4>=1/5. A transience certificate below p=0.17 does not improve this.

verify_marks.fact: With i.i.d. Poisson(mu) sleeping frogs per non-root vertex, critical mu grows linearly in d.
verify_marks.citation: Johnson–Junge arXiv:1607.07914, Theorem 1: 0.24d <= mu_c(d) <= 2.28d for sufficiently large d; HJJ arXiv:1501.05874 Theorem 1 supplies the critical value.

verify_marks.fact: Mathews S_m is the supremum of ordinary-model critical drifts p_d over d>=m, not the self-similar critical drift.
verify_marks.citation: arXiv:2309.14443v2, manuscript p. 2: definition of p_d and S_m.

status_note: No settlement located. Latest explicit primary discussion inspected: Poly Mathews Jr., arXiv:2309.14443v2, introduction p. 2, published ECP 29 (2024). This is a bounded literature-status finding, not an exhaustive proof of present-day openness.

excluded_recent_variant.citation: Angel, de la Riva, Hermon, Shi, arXiv:2512.06640, revised September 2026
excluded_recent_variant.reason: Abstract studies Poisson frogs with a fixed finite lifetime in continuous time and survival/sharpness; it is not the immortal one-frog recurrence question.

limitations: OpenAlex title and DOI requests returned HTTP 429 twice; Semantic Scholar citations request returned HTTP 429. Citing-paper coverage is incomplete.
Broad arXiv queries search metadata and returned unrelated biological papers; absence of a hit is not evidence of a theorem.
The journal DOI page returned an anti-bot/access placeholder (1164 bytes), so theorem content is attributed to the arXiv PDF actually inspected. Crossref verifies publication metadata only.
root_convention: Primary sources use one active root frog and one sleeping frog per non-root vertex. The list text also says a sleeper at the root. A finite extra root seed does not alter the recurrence/transience classification; if needed justify by union of seed-reachable activation closures.
